---


Healf has built a strong position in one of consumer health's fastest-growing categories. The e-commerce wellbeing platform is a trusted place to buy everything from supplements to health tech, and it is now expanding internationally while building out a new "wellbeing intelligence" offering.


Harry R leads People operations at Healf, a role he stepped into in August last year. As the business scales across markets and launches new product lines, his focus has been on building People systems that can keep pace: automated, reliable, and underpinned by data the whole organisation can trust.


> "The automations and AI I've built around Humaans are essential to how we operate. If it disappeared today, it would be terrifying."


Harry R, People Manager, Healf


## Healf at a glance


- **Sector:** E-commerce / health & wellbeing
- **Headquarters:** London, UK
- **Locations:** UK, with international expansion underway (live in Germany, Europe next)
- **HR tech stack:** Humaans (+ Humaans API Custom Tooling), Ashby, n8n, Claude, Slack, Google Workspace


## Key results


- Supports company-wide People operations through rapid growth and international expansion, from the UK to a new market launch in Germany
- Automated onboarding and account provisioning saves around 15 minutes per new hire, roughly two hours for a cohort of eight
- Bulk team restructures, such as renaming teams and moving people, completed in minutes via the Humaans MCP and Claude
- Headcount planning and salary budgeting powered by live Humaans data pulled straight into Claude
- A custom-built performance system connected to Humaans via the API, with joiner and leaver changes and team structures syncing automatically
- A single, secure source of truth for all people data, with role-based permissions across the business


## Building People operations for a global, growing business


Healf is on a mission to help people take charge of their own wellbeing. "We've become the go-to destination for people to shop for trusted products to help empower their wellbeing."


Healf's priorities are clear: keep growing in the UK, expand across Europe (the company just went live in Germany, its first international market), and build out the wellbeing intelligence product. Each of those goals means more people, more locations, and more complexity for the People function to absorb without slowing the business down.


The way to keep pace, Harry knew, was to automate relentlessly and stay close to clean, trusted data. With Humaans as Healf's system of record, the fundamentals are handled, which is exactly what frees the team up for higher-value work. Whether it is a notice period, a salary, or someone's full salary history, "it's all in one place, and I can grab it really easily. I couldn't imagine going back."


## A single source of truth the whole business can trust


Harry pulls information three ways: a quick MCP call in Claude for smaller questions, the reports feature for anything payroll-related, and a straight profile search for contracts. Relevant details surface on their own, too. "I really like that it surfaces things like anniversaries, birthdays and probations, and now it can even surface them in Slack, which makes a lot of difference."


One feature he admits he takes for granted is documents and e-signatures. "It might sound small, but I use it pretty much every day," he says. "I drop in a document, it auto-populates with the employee's information, and once they've signed it links straight to their profile. Imagine doing all that manually on DocuSign, then downloading it and attaching it. It would be such a headache. It's an incredible time save."


And when he exports data, it holds up. "I've never had any issue exporting a report. I pick a template, tick the boxes I need, export a CSV and pull it into Google Sheets. Everything's there."


## Putting AI to work, safely, through Humaans


The People team owns AI enablement across the company, running a cohort-based programme that meets people wherever they are, from beginners to more advanced builders. Harry is one of four leaders driving that work, and Humaans sits at the centre of how he applies AI day to day, in two ways.


The first is workflows. "A couple of days before someone joins, a workflow shoots out an email with all the information we need to create the onboarding documentation for someone," he explains. "That triggers an integration with n8n, which automates the rest: onboarding documentation, a welcome email, the right calendar invites for their first week, their laptop request, provisioning their accounts." The time adds up. "It might only be 15 minutes per new joiner, but if you're hiring eight people in a week, that's two hours I can spend on something else."


The second is the Humaans MCP. "In my Claude terminal I often make MCP calls to Humaans," Harry says. "We've done a lot of work on headcount planning and salary budgeting for the year ahead, and being able to pull that data straight from Humaans and mix it with whatever else I need has been hugely valuable." It works in the other direction too. "When we restructured and spun up a new wellbeing intelligence team, I could let claude know what i needed to do and it made sense of it all in Humaans. Doing it manually would have taken a while. This was so much easier."


Crucially, none of this comes at the expense of security, and for Harry that is a big part of the appeal. "There's always talk of, 'why don't we just build our own HRIS in Claude?' But what I love about a platform like Humaans is that I always know the data is secure. If I built something myself, it could end with everyone finding out personal data about each other. With Humaans, I trust that everything's safe, so as more people interact with it through the MCP, say to book holiday in Claude, I know they're not going to gain access to anything sensitive."


Permissions reinforce that confidence. "Permissions are really straightforward. I love that you can create custom roles, and I always take a least-privilege approach, so people get the minimum they need. It's really easy to change them, and I trust everything's in the right place."


## Extending the platform through the Humaans API


More recently, the team took that approach a step further. Using Claude Code, they built their own performance system to run self-reflections, reviews and priority-setting, designed from the ground up to fit the way Healf works. Rather than standing apart as a separate tool, it connects directly to Humaans through the API.


> "It connects with Humaans so that every time someone joins or leaves, it updates our performance system for seamless data flow," Harry says. "It also groups people correctly based on the teams and departments already set in Humaans, so we didn't have to double up on any work, which saved a lot of time."


Because Humaans remains the system of record, the performance system inherits an accurate, current view of the organisation without manual upkeep. Joiners and leavers flow through automatically, and the existing team structure carries across intact.


## Built to scale as Healf goes global


As Healf grows across Europe and brings wellbeing intelligence to life, Harry sees room to get even more out of the platform, and wants more of his colleagues to discover what it can do. "People often see Humaans as just the place their contract sits, but it can do so much more: workflows to ping your team, assign tasks, manage priorities, even an AI Companion that can answer questions from your company documentation. There are so many valuable features people just aren't using yet."


Asked how he would describe Humaans, his answer is straightforward. "Humaans does everything we need in a really simple way. It feels switched on when it comes to AI and integrations, whether that's Google Workspace, Ashby, or anything else, and workflows are something I haven't really seen any other HRIS do. It feels fresh and modern, and the design is just lovely. Every button makes sense, and it's never overwhelming."


What he returns to, though, is the people behind the product. "The team at Humaans is so lovely. Whether it's a webinar, some documentation, or jumping on a quick call, nothing's ever too much. That support has made a huge difference."


> "They really put the human in Humaans."
